label: Node.js
summary: A Node.js application from git, with node_modules in the release, run with its start command behind Caddy. A frontend (React, Vue, Astro…) is built beforehand and shipped as its output (e.g. dist/).

items: Your content is a git branch or an uploaded package. It is inspected, then goes live within about 2 minutes.
If a new release fails inspection or does not answer, the last good release stays live.
Nothing is built on the server: ship everything the app needs in the release. Include `node_modules` and the built frontend (for example `dist/`).
Read settings with `process.env`; the site's secrets file is loaded into the app's environment.
Persistent files go in `/srv/site/data` (the rest is read-only).
Files your app writes (uploads) must go in data folders, which an installer sets up for your site: they are kept across releases and backed up. Every push replaces the release itself.
The app listens on `127.0.0.1:3000` behind Caddy: your start command (default `npm start`) must listen on `$HOST` and `$PORT`.

hint: a Node.js app with no database
